text:
sasha: Heads-up — while bringing up Anthem's adapter (stitchback) on int4 we saw a small class of failures: amounts and invoice numbers get munged in templates. quick probe please? :thinking_face:
jon: can you drop a minimal prompt + both outputs (fp16 vs int4)?
sasha: pasted below — fp16 looks fine, int4 flips some digits and sometimes drops leading zeros.
sasha: ```
Prompt: 'Generate invoice: id=000123, total=$2,450.00, due=2024-06-15'
FP16 output: 'Invoice id=000123, total $2,450.00, due June 15, 2024'
INT4 output: 'Invoice id=123, total $2,45.00, due 2024-6-15'
```
kevin: ugh. that smells like tokenizer remap + quantized rounding when model relies on special token positions. did we run the stitchback with the customer's tokenizer mapping?
maya: @kevin i ran the merge with our default remap script (stitchback v2) — Anthem's fine-tune added a prefix token set for invoice tokens. maybe those token ids shifted during quantization conversion.
jon: can we replicate locally with `runtest --pack anthem-quickprobe --quant int4 --seed 42`?
sasha: started the local run now, ETA ~3m. I'll paste diff logs when done.
sasha: run finished. eval-bot quick summary attached.
eval-bot: quick-eval results for anthem-quickprobe (seed 42):
- BLEU: fp16 0.72, int4 0.69 (-4.2%)
- Exact-match for invoice-id: fp16 0.995, int4 0.872 (-12.3%)
- Token-shift rate (leading-zero): int4 6.1% vs fp16 0.2%
- Top-1 token-change hotspots: token_id 3124 ("0"), token_id 8871 ("00")
kevin: those hotspots line up with the custom tokenizer additions. looks like some newly inserted tokens have ids near the low-frequency bucket that got clipped in quant kernel selection.
jon: possible mitigations: 1) remap tokenizer so invoice tokens are contiguous in a high-precision id range before quant; 2) force per-channel quant on final linear; 3) soft-fallback to fp16 for lines matching invoice template.
maya: i can try a quick remap patch and re-run int4 conversion. if that fixes it, we ship a note to Anthem about token-id stability requirement for adapters.
sasha: +1 to remap first. please also run a small canary across 50 real customer prompts to ensure no regressed decimal formatting.
maya: kicked off remap + int4-conversion (stitchback-remap-2024-06-15) — will post logs.
kevin: also add a small eval that checks numeric entity LM-likelihood drop: run `compute_likelihood --span invoice-id --model int4` so we can quantify calibration shift.
sasha: added that to the pack. early results: likelihood drop ~1.8 nats on invoice-id span — consistent with token-change.
jon: if remap fails, alternate plan: keep adapter-stitch in int4 but tag routes; route invoice-generation requests to fp16 variant via smart-routing policy (low-volume heuristic).
maya: tests done — remap reduced token-shift rate to 0.6% and exact-match for invoice-id to 0.988. BLEU delta now -0.8%.
sasha: nice. can you commit the remap patch and create a quickpack for Canary rollout (anthem-stitchback-remap-rc1)?
maya: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/anthem-stitchback-remap/pull/12 — includes before/after eval artifact and conversion script.
eval-bot: artifact links: s3://evals/anthem/rc1/results.json, s3://evals/anthem/rc1/diffs.txt
kevin: remind me to add a note in the onboarding checklist: "validate token-id stability after adapter merges". saved us here. :memo:
jon: agrees. also add a regression test to the quickpack that asserts leading-zero preservation for numeric spans.
sasha: thanks team. i'll ping customer success with the plan: remap -> canary -> monitor. will loop back if we see anything else. :thumbsup:
